candidate.name: Last Accounting Company
candidate.description:
Last Accounting Company (LAC) is a full-stack AI accounting firm. We sell the same service (bookkeeping, tax filings, etc.) as a traditional accounting firm, but underneath agents handle everything and a certified accountant signs off. Our service is faster, cheaper, and fully integrated, allowing our clients to focus on what matters, not accounting admin.

LAC replaces both outsourced accountants and legacy accounting software for startups and SMBs. Our system is fully proprietary, from the general ledger to the accounting agents. This allows us to create powerful self-reinforcing loops and ultimately provide a state-of-the-art accounting service.

team: Last Accounting Company was founded by a four-person team in Helsinki: Riki Karjalainen and Sami Laakkonen, who previously built financial data infrastructure at Token Terminal, alongside Veikko Pere (background in BCG, private equity at Intera Partners, and degrees in Finance and Law) and Pietari Virkkunen (background in tech, PE, and VC).
product: A full-stack accounting service where automated AI agents handle routine bookkeeping, payroll reporting, bank reconciliations, and VAT filings, before a certified human accountant reviews and signs off on the final financial statements.
market: Targets Finnish startups, scaleups, and SMBs who currently pay recurring fees to outsourced accounting firms alongside legacy accounting software subscriptions. Agentic LLMs and API integrations now make end-to-end reconciliation and document parsing viable without manual data entry.
risks: Accounting errors or statutory tax misfilings could trigger significant professional liability and churn client trust.
Heavy localization to Finnish banking integrations and tax rules creates friction when attempting to expand internationally.
Reliance on human accountant sign-offs could create an operational bottleneck that compresses gross margins as client volume scales.
open_questions: How many paying clients currently rely on LAC for their active monthly close and official tax filings?
Are the certified accountants signing off on filings employed full-time in-house or outsourced contractors?
What percentage of ledger transactions currently require human intervention versus full end-to-end automation?
